children: Sterling is little moved after data showed the U.K. economy unexpectedly grew, albeit only slightly, in August. Gross domestic product rose 0.1% month-on-month in August after a 0.4% increase in July. Economists in a WSJ survey had expected a 0.1% fall in GDP. The data are unlikely to materially change the thinking of the Bank of England ahead of November's decision where markets already almost fully price a 25 basis-point interest-rate rise, Omnis Investments strategist Patrick O'Donnell says in a note. Sterling rises 0.3% to $1.3232 versus a stronger dollar but falls 0.1% to 0.8463 per euro, both little changed from levels before the data. (renae.dyer@wsj.com)
